ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a 5×5 grid. P is located in the upper-left square, namely row 1 column 1; Q is located in the lower-right square, namely row 5 column 5. Thick black obstacles are drawn on the common edges of several adjacent squares: from the figure, they can be read as blocking movement downward from (2,2), downward from (2,3), rightward from (3,3), downward from (3,4), rightward from (2,4), rightward from (4,1), and downward from (4,2). Reasoning: From P=(1,1) to Q=(5,5), the shortest route needs a total of 4 steps to the right and 4 steps downward, so it is only necessary to count monotone paths that avoid the blocked edges. Let ways(i,j) be the number of shortest paths reaching row i column j, ways(1,1)=1. The number of paths for each square comes from above and from the left, but if the corresponding common edge is blocked by an obstacle, then it is not added. Fill the table row by row: Row 1: 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 Row 2: 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, where (2,4) to (2,5) is blocked, so (2,5) cannot come from the left, and can only come from above. Row 3: 1, 1, 1, 4, 5, where downward from (2,2) and (2,3) is blocked, and rightward from (3,3) is blocked. Row 4: 1, 1, 2, 2, 7, where rightward from (4,1) is blocked, and downward from (3,4) is blocked. Row 5: 1, 1, 3, 5, 12, where downward from (4,2) is blocked. So the number of shortest paths reaching Q=(5,5) is ways(5,5)=12.

raw_record.question_text: Max and Moritz have drawn out a $5 \times 5$ grid on the playground, together with three obstacles. They want to walk from $P$ to $Q$ using the shortest route, avoiding the obstacles and always crossing a common edge to go from the centre of one square to the centre of the next. How many such shortest paths are there from $P$ to $Q$?

method.method_draft: Label the 5 by 5 squares by row and column, with P at cell (1,1) and Q at cell (5,5), as read from the image. Treat each thick black segment as blocking movement across that grid edge: down from (2,2) and (2,3), right from (3,3), down from (3,4), right from (2,4), right from (4,1), and down from (4,2). From the text, shortest paths from P to Q must use only 4 moves right and 4 moves down, because P is top-left and Q is bottom-right. Use dynamic programming on the cells: set ways(1,1)=1, and for every other cell add the number of ways from the cell above and from the cell to the left, except when the shared edge is one of the blocked obstacle edges. Filling the table gives ways(5,5)=12.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图显示一个 5×5 方格。P 位于左上角方格，即第1行第1列；Q 位于右下角方格，即第5行第5列。粗黑障碍物画在若干相邻方格的公共边上：从图中可读为阻挡从(2,2)向下、从(2,3)向下、从(3,3)向右、从(3,4)向下、从(2,4)向右、从(4,1)向右、从(4,2)向下的移动。

推理：从P=(1,1)到Q=(5,5)，最短路线需要总共向右4步、向下4步，因此只需统计避开被阻挡边的单调路径。设ways(i,j)为到达第i行第j列的最短路径数，ways(1,1)=1。每个格子的路径数来自上方和左方，但若对应公共边被障碍阻挡，则不加入。

逐行填表：
第1行：1, 1, 1, 1, 1
第2行：1, 2, 3, 4, 1，其中(2,4)到(2,5)被挡，所以(2,5)不能从左方来，只能从上方来。
第3行：1, 1, 1, 4, 5，其中(2,2)和(2,3)向下被挡，(3,3)向右被挡。
第4行：1, 1, 2, 2, 7，其中(4,1)向右被挡，(3,4)向下被挡。
第5行：1, 1, 3, 5, 12，其中(4,2)向下被挡。

所以到达Q=(5,5)的最短路径数是ways(5,5)=12。
